map.headline: What do you want to experience?
map.first: Most of it built by hand, for one summer only.
map.architecture: Built by hand each summer, then given away.
map.phoneFirst: Pick one below to light up the map, or see all 20 neighborhoods.

XPD.Architecture: Built by hand each summer, then given away to schools, farms and woodworkers.
XPD.Music: Find your next favorite band in a forest bowl, an old barn or a meadow at sunset.
XPD.DJs: Dance under the trees until the stars come out, and long after.
XPD.Family: Kids 12 and under get in free, and get a camp of their own in the woods.
XPD.Comedy: Touring comics on a barn stage, with a crowd close enough to heckle.
XPD.Literary: Slow down for stories and poems, read aloud beneath the trees.
XPD.Wellness: Morning yoga, sound baths, forest hikes and a sober-friendly place to rest.
XPD.Food: Sit down at a long table by the creek, or eat your way through local kitchens.
XPD.Craft: Meet the makers and take home something made by hand.
XPD.Drinks: Local beer, wine, cocktails and coffee, never far from a stage.
XPD.Art: Installations that come alive after dark, and murals painted while you watch.
XPD.Camping: Sleep under giant firs and ferns, or in your own rig, and walk in to the music.

desc.woods: A steep trail drops into a natural bowl ringed by Douglas firs, under a roof of big-leaf maples. Shaded all day, it runs from morning until late at night, and its stage is rebuilt each year from the forest around it.
desc.paddock: The only place on the farm big enough to hold everyone at once. It opens after the sun drops behind the tree line, and its edge is redrawn every year.
desc.cherryhill: The dark sister of the Woods, asleep by day and glowing on the ridge at night. Portland State architecture students build it from borrowed materials, then send them back to work.
desc.grove: A dense stand of Douglas firs that stays cool all day, where the stage weaves through the trunks and art hides in the shade.
desc.windmill: A hillside lounge on the forest edge above the meadow, under tall firs and the farm's old windmill. Readings and coffee in the morning, punk and records by afternoon.
desc.galaxy: A century-old barn where the line between band and crowd disappears. Psych, punk and soul you feel in your chest.
desc.lucky: A barn with seats for sets that need a quieter room, with shade and a hundred seats outside for the wait.
desc.farmhouse: The front door to the farm: rideshare, shuttle and bikes arrive here, wristbands go on, and the first music of the day greets you.
desc.curation: A room just off the farm, beside the creek, where one chef and one band share a table with a hundred people, from Friday dinner to Sunday brunch.
desc.refuge: A protected pocket of the farm for rest: yoga, sound baths, plant meditation, tarot, and a sober-friendly place to land. Cedar showers are tucked in the trees.
desc.coyote: A camp of their own for kids, with kid bands, puppet parades, crafts and drop-off care. Kids 12 and under get in free.
desc.courtyard: The open-air plaza outside the Galaxy Barn, with a fire pit, a bar and a screen showing the stage inside. Its lumber goes on to Oregon woodworkers.
desc.market: The town square, where every path crosses: Oregon kitchens, a dozen makers, a bar, a seating shed and a pop-up dance floor, with art that wakes up at night.
desc.orchard: A hallway of old apple trees from the front door down to the barns, where the outside world starts to fade.
desc.welcomelot: The first stop for drivers: wristbands through the car window, gear drop-off, then a mile's walk through the woods or a shuttle to the gate.
desc.quailtrail: A wooded path of art between the Woods and the heart of the farm.
desc.lushcamp: The big central campground, shaded and full of ferns, close to the stages, with a quiet camp for families.
desc.wildcamp: Rugged camping in the upper reaches of the property, among the biggest trees on the farm.
desc.willowcamp: Field camping for cars, vans and RVs under a huge willow, a short shuttle or half-mile walk from the gates.
desc.southcamp: Vehicle camping right beside the main entrance, for anyone who wants their rig close.
